gaps.sentence: Please ___ me to post this letter.
gaps.hint: make somebody not forget: ___ somebody to do something
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody to do something' means to make someone remember; 'remember' is something you do yourself.

gaps.sentence: Look at that bird up ___ in the tree.
gaps.explanation: 'There' refers to a place; 'their' shows possession; 'they're' means 'they are'.

gaps.sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
gaps.hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
gaps.explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.

gaps.sentence: The new law will ___ every driver in the country.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to have an influence on; 'effect' is normally a noun meaning a result.
'Besides' means in addition to; 'beside' means next to; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: He should be ___ of himself for lying to his friends.
gaps.hint: feeling guilt about something you did; pattern: ___ of
gaps.explanation: 'Ashamed of' means feeling guilt or shame about behaviour; 'embarrassed' is only social discomfort.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.
